title: POC Weekly Sync - App Integration / SDK / Tool & Function Calls
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest inference results integrated into Oceanic's payments app. Discussed SDK integration for tool/function calls, structured output schema, performance numbers (latency and cost), and remaining security gating items. Agreed next steps include SDK sample updates, a 1k-request benchmark run, and sharing security/compliance docs and network diagram.
next_steps: Alex to share updated SDK sample repo and README (includes tool call examples)
Oceanic to run 1k synthetic benchmark on staging using the provided config and report latency percentiles
Redwood to share SOC2 summary + network diagram + sample KMS integration guide
Schedule follow-up deep-dive on routing/fallback policies if benchmark shows >150ms p95
action_items: Alex Chen: Send updated SDK sample and README (due: 2026-09-14)
Raj Mehta: Run 1,000-request benchmark in staging and upload results (due: 2026-09-16)
Samir Patel: Provide guidance for structured-output validation and a JSON schema example (due: 2026-09-13)
Alex Chen: Share SOC2 summary, network diagram, and KMS notes (due: 2026-09-11)
Priya Nair: Confirm success criteria for POC (latency p95 < 150ms, cost per 1k tokens target) (due: 2026-09-15)
transcript: [00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We've got about 38 minutes blocked - quick check-in, run through results, and next steps.
[00:12] Emma Rodriguez: Thanks Alex, yep. We rolled a small build to staging last night. Want to go over the integration notes, see where the structured output landed and any tweaks to SDK calls.
[00:25] Samir Patel: Great. I pulled the logs from your staging key earlier this morning, saw a couple of function-call hits and a few JSON schema mismatches - we'll cover those.

[00:40] Raj Mehta: Quick context - our integration uses the Redwood SDK via the node client, we proxy calls through an internal service that augments prompts with payment metadata. Main questions: how do we best do tool calling to trigger the payment microservice? And how do we statically validate the structured output before applying state changes?

[01:10] Jordan Lee: For tool/function calls, the SDK supports declared functions in the request payload; the LLM can return a function call object. We recommend server-side canonicalization: validate the returned args with a JSON schema, then map to your internal RPC. That avoids trusting model text directly.

[01:35] Priya Nair: We had one case where the model returned an extra field - like amount_usd_str instead of amount_cents - that broke our deserialization. Is there a pattern to force a strict schema?

[01:50] Samir Patel: Yeah we've seen that. Two patterns: 1) use Redwood's structured output helpers (SDK has a validateResponse helper) which returns a normalized object or error, and 2) include explicit output schema in the prompt + function signature so the model is nudged to produce exact fields. We'll share the schema sample.
[02:20] Emma Rodriguez: When you say SDK validateResponse, is that on the client or the Redwood side? We're trying to keep as little code in the path as possible due to latency concerns.
[02:35] Alex Chen: The helper runs client-side in your service - lightweight JSON validation. It adds ~2-5ms. The heavy lifting (function call routing) is still done by your service after validation.

[02:50] Liam O'Connor: About latency - our SLO is p95 under 150ms for in-app flows. The last run in staging read ~180ms p95 when we hit a cold KV cache. Any advice on caching and batching with Redwood to improve that?

[03:10] Samir Patel: Sure. Two levers: enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts and use continuous batching on the Dedicated pool if you're on Reserved. For Hosted, caching plus sticky routing to a low-latency region helps. Also quantization can reduce compute time but may affect output quality - we can tune per workload.
[03:40] Raj Mehta: We're on hosted for the POC. Is sticky routing something we can configure from the console or via the API?

[03:50] Alex Chen: Both. Console has a route to prefer region/us-west, and the API request can include a routing_hint header. For POC we usually set routing in the console and validate in the benchmark.
[04:05] Emma Rodriguez: About cost - Priya flagged that token spend spiked on Friday. Any quick wins to reduce unit cost without impacting accuracy?

[04:18] Samir Patel: Common wins: shorter prompt templates, prefix caching, and moving some heavy context to embeddings + retrieval instead of full prompt. You can also choose a lighter model variant for deterministic tool calls and keep a higher-quality model for hallucination-prone tasks.
[04:40] Priya Nair: For the POC we need reproducible results for payments decisions - deterministic output matters. Is there a recommended model or config?

[04:55] Jordan Lee: Use a tuned model variant with temperature ~0.0 for function calls. Redwood has a baseline that we've verified for structured outputs; we'll point you to the model id in the sample.

[05:12] Raj Mehta: On the point about model ids - earlier our logs had the model name slightly mangled (it logged as redwood-bison instead of redwood-bison-v2) so our telemetry mapping broke. Any tips to keep logs consistent?
[05:28] Alex Chen: Yeah transcription/mapping issues happen. We recommend logging both model_id and the runtime_build version from the response metadata - we'll include that in the sample code.
[05:45] Emma Rodriguez: Can you walk us through the sample SDK call you suggested? We looked at the repo but wanted to see a real request/response flow for function calls.

[05:55] Samir Patel: Sure I'll read out a trimmed snippet - it's nodejs but similar in other SDKs. (paraphrase) client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'redwood-structured-v1', messages: [...], functions: [{name:'create_payment', parameters: {...}}], temperature: 0.0, validate_schema: true }) - response contains choices[0].function_call.name and .arguments as JSON string.
[06:40] Raj Mehta: And the validate_schema flag does the helper validation?
[06:47] Samir Patel: Correct. If validation fails it'll return a structured error and you can fallback to a manual confirmation flow.

[06:58] Priya Nair: We ran into a failure where the model returned the correct intent but used 'usd_amount' instead of 'amount_cents' and validate_schema failed. Do you recommend auto-mapping heuristics or strict fail?
[07:13] Jordan Lee: For payments you want strict fail and human-in-the-loop confirmation. For lower-risk flows, you can include heuristics with confidence thresholds.
[07:30] Emma Rodriguez: Security checklist - last week we asked about VPC, KMS, and audit logs. Where are we on those artifacts?

[07:40] Alex Chen: I have the SOC2 summary and a network diagram ready to send after the call. For KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed keys; we'll attach the KMS integration notes. Audit logs are available via the console with export to your S3 bucket or SIEM.
[07:55] Liam O'Connor: Does the audit export include token-level provenance and redaction controls? We need to ensure PHI/PPI tokens aren't stored in plain text.
[08:07] Samir Patel: We redact sensitive fields by default for hosted logs and offer field-level redaction configs in Private deployments. We'll include recommended config examples.
[08:25] Raj Mehta: Back to performance - in the staging run we saw p50 ~ 85ms, p95 ~ 180ms. The tail seems spiky. Any quick tracing tips to figure whether it's model runtime vs network?
[08:40] Jordan Lee: Add the runtime tracing hook in the SDK; it returns breakdowns: request serialize, network, runtime-token-generation, and KV cache hits. We can correlate to pinpoint.
[08:55] Emma Rodriguez: Samir, can you confirm that hooking that trace doesn't add significant overhead?
[09:02] Samir Patel: It adds negligible overhead - it's async and batched. We'll provide a short snippet to enable it.

[09:15] Priya Nair: On the structured output format - we want to enforce an enum for payment_method and include nested object for beneficiary with name and bank_id. Any best practices for schema design?

[09:30] Jordan Lee: Flatten when possible - nested schemas are fine but make sure the schema validators on your side accept both numbers and strings with canonicalizers. We'll share a recommended schema with examples.
[09:45] Raj Mehta: Regarding retries and idempotency - when a function call fails mid-flow, what's Redwood's recommended approach to avoid double-payments?

[09:58] Alex Chen: Make your payment RPC idempotent using client-supplied idempotency keys and validate the function_call.arguments for a unique request_id. Redwood doesn't execute your backend payment; it just returns structured args.

[10:15] Emma Rodriguez: For the benchmark we want to replicate real app traffic shape - mostly short chat messages with function calls ~40% of the time. Any configs we should use to get realistic routing?

[10:30] Samir Patel: Use the batch config in the benchmark manifest and include variable inter-arrival times. We'll share the sample bench manifest (it includes routing_hint, model, and validate_schema toggles).
[10:45] Priya Nair: On the cost side again - do you provide cost breakdown per-route? So we can see token cost vs function-call overhead?
[10:55] Alex Chen: Yes Console shows per-route cost and token breakdown, and we can export a CSV with line items. For POC we can run a short export to help estimate monthly run rate.

[11:10] Raj Mehta: One more on tool calling - suppose model calls 'create_payment' but also suggests a follow-up 'verify_kyc' call in the same response. Is chain-of-tools supported or do we need to run sequentially?

[11:24] Jordan Lee: The model can request multiple function calls, but best practice is to process them sequentially and re-invoke the model if you need the next decision step. We don't recommend firing multiple side-effectful RPCs without validation in between.
[11:40] Emma Rodriguez: Ok makes sense. Any known gotchas when integrating with our event-sourced payments system?
[11:50] Samir Patel: Ensure your event publisher is idempotent and that you persist intermediate states. Also, we recommend including trace ids from Redwood in your events for easier correlation.
[12:05] Priya Nair: Can Redwood's SDK attach trace ids automatically?
[12:12] Alex Chen: Yes the SDK returns a request_id header and you can pass correlation_id in the request metadata; we'll show the exact header names in the sample.
[12:25] Raj Mehta: We also had a couple of malformed JSON responses in the last run - is it likely model noise or an SDK parsing bug?

[12:34] Samir Patel: Likely model output formatting; the SDK attempts to parse function_call.arguments as JSON but if the model returns trailing commas or quotes it can fail. The validate_schema helper handles some of this via tolerant parsing, but you'll see errors logged - we'll include a debug flag to dump raw model output for triage.
[12:55] Emma Rodriguez: Next, security review - we plan to have our security team review the SOC2 docs. When can you send them?
[13:02] Alex Chen: I'll email the SOC2 summary and network diagram right after this call. Also adding the KMS integration doc.
[13:12] Liam O'Connor: One more item from ops - outbound IP ranges for Hosted API for allowlisting?
[13:20] Samir Patel: We've got a list of regional egress IP ranges. For production you can use Dedicated or Private to avoid IP variability. We'll attach the IP CIDRs.
[13:33] Priya Nair: On deadlines - steering committee wants a POC decision by end of next sprint (two weeks). What should we deliver to make the case?

[13:45] Alex Chen: Deliverables: 1) benchmarking report with p50/p95 and cost estimates, 2) a short demo of end-to-end payment flow with structured validation, 3) security artifacts. If those look good, we can propose next steps to pilot on a subset of users.
[14:02] Raj Mehta: We'll try to prioritize the benchmark and the demo. The staging run last night hit a few JSON schema mismatches - Samir will you send the schema example?
[14:12] Samir Patel: Yep, I'll paste the schema and a small nodejs snippet using ajv for validation.

[14:20] Jordan Lee: Also note, if you hit hallucinations on beneficiary fields, try adding a retrieval step for beneficiary IDs from your data store before calling the function - supply the model with canonical data.
[14:34] Emma Rodriguez: Good call. One question on logs retention - how long are transcripts and audit logs kept?
[14:40] Alex Chen: Hosted default is 90 days, configurable for enterprise accounts. For Dedicated/Private we can adjust retention per contract.
[14:52] Priya Nair: Any immediate blockers from Redwood's side for us to run the benchmark?

[14:58] Samir Patel: No blockers. We'll send the bench manifest, SDK snippets, schema, and security docs. The only thing we need from you is the staging access key and confirmation on the traffic shape.
[15:15] Raj Mehta: We'll provision a staging key and run the 1k synthetic test with the batch profile Alex mentioned.
[15:25] Emma Rodriguez: Great. Let's recap action items before we close.

[15:30] Alex Chen: Recap: I'll send SDK sample, SOC2 summary, network diagram, KMS notes, and bench manifest. Samir will add schema and validation snippet. Raj will run the benchmark and share results. Priya to confirm success criteria. We'll reconvene after bench results; if p95 < 150ms we'll move to pilot planning.
[15:55] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Anything else?
[16:00] Liam O'Connor: One tiny ask - include sample logs with the runtime trace breakdown so we can instrument similarly.
[16:08] Jordan Lee: Will include that in the sample repo.
[16:15] Emma Rodriguez: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[16:18] Alex Chen: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the materials. Bye.
[38:00] Meeting end
